name: Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Ltd
title: Sri Lotus Developers and Realty Ltd - 544469 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Q4 FY26 pre-sales rose 177% YoY to INR462 crores, but collections were only INR82 crores against INR308 crores revenue.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 pre-sales of INR462 crores (up 177% YoY), revenue of INR308 crores (up 62% YoY) and PAT of INR101 crores (up 17% YoY). FY26 pre-sales were INR1,157 crores (up 137%), revenue INR769 crores (up 40%) and PAT INR243 crores. Collections remained weak at INR82 crores in Q4 and INR376 crores for FY26, which management attributed to all four newly launched projects being in basement stage. Management guided FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores with revenue and PAT growth of 55-60%, and a launch pipeline of six projects worth INR5,000-5,500 crores GDV.

segments.name: Residential (ultra-luxury, Mumbai)
segments.commentary: Lotus Celestia (Versova) booked INR155 crores within 7 days of March 2026 launch, GDV INR1,400-1,500 crores. Amalfi sold about 61-62% and The Arcadian 41%, Varun 38% within a year of launch.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Two new commercial projects in Andheri West to launch in H1 FY27 (Lotus Sky Plaza and Lotus Trident); management expects 10-20% pricing premium to rivals.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance INR1,800-2,000 crores, revenue growth 55-60% and PAT growth 55-60%.
Six planned launches (Aquaria, Trident, Aurelia, Sky Plaza, Portofino, Odyssey) with GDV INR5,000-5,500 crores; three launches in H1 FY27 with combined revenue potential INR2,500-3,000 crores.
Project cost inflation estimated at about 1% annualised; management also cited a 1.5-2.5% range for total project cost.
Margins expected to remain in the guided range despite marketing spend below 1% of revenue.
Collections expected to improve in Q1 and H1 FY27 as projects move from basement to plinth and superstructure.
Target to sign four to six new projects in the coming year.
Dividend payout of 50% for FY26 approved; promoter group waived its FY26 dividend. Company is formulating a dividend policy.
capex_capacity: Aquaria (Prabhadevi): 100% approvals, work started, launch planned this quarter.
Trident: full approvals, launch planned this quarter.
Sky Plaza (Andheri): about 80% approvals obtained, H1 FY27 launch.
Remaining three H2 launches expected to get all approvals in Q1 FY27 with launch the following quarter.
Lotus Monarch, Lotus Avalon and Lotus Solana delayed; one project needs a separate hospital to be built before sale area is separated.
Net IPO proceeds of about INR732 crores (fresh issue INR792 crores gross); INR394 crores deployed till March 2026.
Projected free cash flow: INR3,103 crores from completed and ongoing projects, INR5,450 crores from upcoming, total INR8,553 crores.
demand_pricing: Management says ultra-luxury (INR10-12 crore+ tickets) demand is strong and insulated from external forces; pricing about 10-20% (up to 25%) above competitors in each micro market.
Nine new projects added in FY26 with cumulative GDV of about INR8,500-9,000 crores.
Q4 pre-sales INR462 crores include INR203 crores from Varun, Arcadian and Amalfi, and INR358 crores from FY26 launches.
Arc One realisations rose after occupation certificate and amenity completion, per management.
Marketing campaign 'Luxury Coastline Collection' covers 11 projects across Versova, Juhu, Carter Road, Bandstand, Prabhadevi and Nepean Sea Road.

qa_highlights.question: Collections are low versus revenue despite milestone-linked billing; when will they pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said collections are low because all four new projects are in basement stage, where expenses are high but customer dues are small; collections are expected to improve in Q1 FY27 and H1 as projects reach plinth and slabs.

qa_highlights.question: Confidence in INR1,800-2,000 crore FY27 pre-sales amid slowdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ultra-luxury demand is strong and that the four existing projects plus six new launches would together deliver about INR1,800 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue recognised from FY26 pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said INR460 crores of revenue was recognised from the INR1,157 crores of FY26 pre-sales, which he described as the Q4 figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Monarch, Avalon and Solana delayed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two projects need multiple approvals, including construction of an existing hospital to separate the sale area.

qa_highlights.question: Cost pressure from geopolitical tensions?
qa_highlights.answer: Input costs rose about 7% and labour about 5%; management estimated total project cost impact at 2-2.5%, with no import component in supply chain.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a dividend policy is being formulated for deliberation at the next board meeting; 50% payout declared for non-promoter shareholders for FY26.

risks_watch: Collections (INR82 crores in Q4 vs INR308 crores revenue) lag recognition; FY26 collections of INR376 crores versus INR769 crores revenue. Watch Q1 FY27 collections as the four new projects reach plinth.
FY27 guidance depends on six launches (INR5,000-5,500 crores GDV) and on approvals for Sky Plaza (about 80%) and the H2 projects; Monarch, Avalon and Solana are already delayed.
Management's cost-inflation figures vary across the call (about 1% annualised versus 1.5-2.5% total project cost), so the margin impact is not clearly quantified.
Ghatkopar matter (about INR600 crores GDV) is pending at the Supreme Court; outcome expected this year.
Q4 PAT growth of 17% was well below the 62% revenue growth; the drivers were not explained on the call.
Management said the dividend policy is still being formulated.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and FY27 targets, with strong statements on ultra-luxury pricing power. Evasive on collections, approval delays and the Ghatkopar matter, and gave limited numerical detail on cost and margin impact.
key_quotes: So we are very confident that we will be able to achieve that.
Fortunately, we do not have any import component in our supply chain.
Pre-sales for Q4 FY26 stood at INR462 crores, registering a strong growth of 177% year-on-year.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores pre-sales and 55-60% revenue and PAT growth, backed by six planned launches (GDV INR5,000-5,500 crores, three in H1 FY27) and strong Q4 pre-sales of INR462 crores, but collections of only INR82 crores and no hard capacity additions, so backing is partial.
